newsitem.title: USA: DUPONT, PIONEER IN CROP RESEARCH VENTURE.
newsitem.headline: DUPONT, PIONEER IN CROP RESEARCH VENTURE.

text.p: DuPont Co and Pioneer Hi-Bred International said they agreed to form a research alliance and separate joint venture company to speed development of new crops.

As part of this agreement, DuPont will invest $1.7 billion in Pioneer, ultimately owning 20 percent of its stock for $104 per share, and will have two of the 15 seats on Pioneer's board of directors, the companies said.
Pioneer will use the proceeds to buy back its own stock, the companies said.
The agreement includes a 16-year standstill and corporate governance agreement, they said.

"This linkage with DuPont will enable Pioneer, as an independent company, to team with a leading agricultural technology provider to meet the changing needs of crop producers and end-users of grain and oilseeds," Charles Johnson, chairman of Pioneer, said in a statement.

The alliance between Pioneer, the number one North American seed corn company, and DuPont follows similar ventures in the growing area of agricultural biotechnology. DeKalb Genetics Corp, the number two seed corn company, has an alliance with Monsanto Co, which has a significant minority stake in DeKalb.

"DuPont and Pioneer will integrate DuPont's recognized strengths in materials sciences and biotechnology with Pioneer's global strength in corn and oilseed genetics to create a new generation of products for agriculture," John Krol, president of DuPont, said in a statement.

They said the alliance will create one of the world's largest private agricultural research and development collaborations. The two companies will collectively invest more than $400 million in agricultural research next year.

A portion of those budgets will support the joint venture directly, with collaborative research in genetic modification of corn, soybeans and other oilseeds to improve their oil, protein and carbohydrate composition.
Both companies said they can apply discoveries and technology gained from the alliance to enhance traditional products, such as hybrid seeds and corp protection products.

The joint venture company, Optimum Quality Grains, will include DuPont Agricultural Products' Quality Grains business and Pioneer's Nutrition Industry Markets business, both based in Des Moines, Iowa.
